newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 13.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* U.S. blue-chip stocks jumped to their fifth straight record closing on Thursday, as bond interest rates tumbled on surprisingly weak economic data that eased concerns about rising interest rates. The Dow Jones industrial average surged 135.64 points to a record 7,711.47.
* The World Trade Organisation (WTO) on Thursday agreed to create a panel to look into complaints from Japan and the European Union that Indonesia's national car policy violates open trading rules.
* On Thursday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 2.18 points, or 0.32 percent higher, at 695.22 points on sustained buying interest in property and banking stocks, brokers said.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,426.50/27.50 at 0125 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,428.50/29.00.
* Blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) after Finance Minister Mari'e Muhammad reportedly confirmed that government is studying the possibility of merging the seven state banks into four entities.
On Monday, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported that BNI will merge with another state bank Bank Tabungan Negara.

* Blue chip telecommunications firm PT Telkom on a report in the Jakarta Post which quoted Telkom director Asman A. Nasution as saying that it is selecting potential partners to run the Digital Cordless System (DCS)-1800 nationwide and Personal Handyphone System in East Java area.

Last week, the government had awarded five new cellular licences, including one each to Telkom and PT Indonesia Satellite (Indosat). In addition to the five new licences, the government last Monday opened the tender process for 11 new licences.
* Bank Papan Sejahtera following reports that the Indonesian central bank will divest its 13.11 percent stake in the bank.
* Confectionery firm Mayora Indah on reports that its planned 300 billion rupiah bond had received an "A "rating from Indonesia's rating agency Pefindo.

* Small financing firm PT Clipan Finance Indonesia CLPI.JK after the exchange body suspended trading in the counter as it rose too sharply. Brokers said the rise was linked to market talk that it was likely to be taken over by another finance firm.
* Cable maker Voksel Electric after the firm said its optical fibre plant will start operations later this year.
